concepts.title: Fundamental Principle of Counting
concepts.definition: The fundamental principle of counting states that if one event can occur in m ways and a second independent event in n ways, then the two together occur in m times n ways, and the rule extends by multiplication to any number of successive choices.
concepts.textbook_ref: Repeated choices from the same set of options over several positions give options raised to the number of positions, as in number plates and codes.

concepts.title: Permutations: Arrangements in Order
concepts.definition: A permutation is an arrangement of objects in a definite order, the number of permutations of n distinct objects taken r at a time is written nPr, and permutations with repetitions use n to the power r, while arrangements of objects with repetitions are counted by dividing by the repeated factorials.
concepts.key_idea: Order matters in permutations, so AB and BA are different arrangements, unlike combinations.

concepts.title: Combinations: Selections Without Order and the Pair Count
concepts.definition: A combination selects r objects from n without regard to order, written nCr, and every pair of objects chosen from n distinct objects gives n times n minus one divided by two selections, since each pair is counted twice in the ordered arrangements.
concepts.textbook_ref: Combinations ignore order, so the number of handshakes among n people equals the number of pairs n times n minus one over two.
